chunks: From him, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no drop more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than a drop of tears shed in the darkness of the night out of fear of Allah, not intending anything else by it.
ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved act of worship to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on weeping, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) underscores the spiritual potency of nocturnal tears shed in sincere khawf (fear of God) without seeking worldly recognition. Shia scholars often link this to the concept of 'sirr' (secret) worship, where the darkness of night symbolizes the purity of intention, making these tears a direct conduit for divine proximity and forgiveness.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Musna Al Hannat, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from a drop more Beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic than a tear drop shed in the darkness of the night fearing from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, not intending anything else by it’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from Muthanna al-Hannat from abu Hamza from abu la’ far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
No drop is more beloved to Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, than the drop of tears in the dark night for fear of Allah, and is intended to be just for Him alone.”
